title: Total Boolean decision problems: a fourth-power bound

problem.name: Total Boolean function evaluation
problem.statement_latex: For a total function $f:\{0,1\}^N\to\{0,1\}$, determine $f(x)$ by accessing individual bits of $x$. Every $N$-bit string is a valid input. Threshold decision versions of explicitly encoded optimization problems are examples. Complexity is measured in input-bit oracle queries, with deterministic classical and bounded-error quantum algorithms distinguished.

quantum.headline_latex: $Q(f)$ queries, an optimal bounded-error quantum decision algorithm.
quantum.headline_text: $Q(f)$ queries, an optimal bounded-error quantum decision algorithm.
quantum.details_latex: The theorem relates this resource to deterministic query complexity for every total Boolean function. In particular, every nonconstant monotone graph property on an $n$-vertex adjacency matrix has quantum query complexity $\Omega(n)$.
quantum.details_text: The theorem relates this resource to deterministic query complexity for every total Boolean function. In particular, every nonconstant monotone graph property on an $n$-vertex adjacency matrix has quantum query complexity $\Omega(n)$.

classical.details_latex: A decision tree achieving this bound exists for every total $f$. Randomized query complexity satisfies $R(f)\le D(f)$. Known total functions attain the fourth-power deterministic-versus-quantum relationship up to logarithmic factors. The resource being bounded is the number of queried input bits; computation on the answers is free in this model.

strength.description_latex: A polynomial upper bound on the possible query advantage, including separations greater than quadratic. The fourth-power relationship concerns deterministic classical complexity.
